subject: Making awkward kitchen spaces useful
hook: None of my walls are straight. Can a fitted kitchen still look right?
fb:
A question we get from lots of people in older houses around Stoke-on-Trent: my walls aren't straight, so will a fitted kitchen look wrong?

It won't. Hardly any walls are perfectly straight or square. We find the bows and slopes at the survey, build the units level in our workshop, then scribe the filler and end panels on site so they follow the shape of the wall.

The units stay true, the panels take up the difference, and you don't get those tapering gaps that give an uneven wall away.

Got an awkward kitchen you'd like a second opinion on? Ask us here or book a free consultation:

gbp:
My walls aren't straight. Can a fitted kitchen still look right?

Yes. Very few walls are perfectly straight or square, particularly in older and extended homes. A good fitted kitchen is designed to cope with that rather than hide it with sealant.

At the measuring visit we check walls at different heights and note any bows, slopes and out-of-square corners. The units themselves are built level and square in our own workshop. On site, our team scribes the filler panels and end panels so they follow the exact line of the wall. The cabinets stay true and the panels take up the difference, so there are no tapering gaps along the worktop or up the side of a tall unit.

The same approach works for fitted wardrobes, media walls and alcove units.

If your kitchen has awkward walls, corners or recesses, book a free, no-obligation design consultation and we'll talk you through what's possible.
